capture.why:
Pins the contract facts the upcoming_recordings backup category rests on. Four of them were NOT knowable from the model/serializer source and two of those would have shipped as defects:
(1) GET /api/channels/recordings/ answers a BARE JSON ARRAY, not a DRF paginated envelope -- same shape as recurring-rules.
(2) Recording has NO status column. The upcoming/completed distinction is NOT a first-class field; custom_properties.status is a free-form JSONField key the DVR pipeline writes ('scheduled' / 'recording' / 'completed' / 'interrupted' / 'stopped'). The only field-level, always-present discriminator is the absolute start_time, which is why ECM's filter is start_time > now -- the same predicate Dispatcharr's OWN BulkDeleteUpcomingRecordingsAPIView uses to mean 'upcoming' (apps/channels/api_views.py: Recording.objects.filter(start_time__gt=now)).
(3) THE DESTINATION REFUSES A PAST-DATED CREATE: posting a recording whose end_time has passed answers 400 {"non_field_errors":["End time must be in the future."]}. A restore that replayed archived absolute timestamps unfiltered would fail every stale row upstream instead of skipping it. ECM's restore-side staleness gate is STRICTER than this (it requires start_time in the future, not merely end_time), so ECM never hands upstream a create this validator would reject.
(4) THE DESTINATION MUTATES custom_properties AFTER THE CREATE: the 201 for id=1 returned custom_properties {} and the GET moments later returned {"poster_logo_id": 316} -- Dispatcharr's own artwork pass wrote it. custom_properties is therefore NOT usable as an identity/collision field. ECM matches on (channel, start_time, end_time) instead.
(5) task_id is server-assigned and read-only ('dvr-recording-<id>'); it is never sent on a create.
(6) The server may normalize start_time to a DIFFERENT STRING than the one posted -- id=3 was posted at second precision and came back as '2026-08-23T23:16:58.511980Z'. Timestamp identity must compare parsed instants, never strings.
capture.known_gap_no_completed_row: No COMPLETED recording is captured here, and none can be: the create validator above rejects any row whose end_time has already passed, so a completed row can only come into existence by a recording actually running to completion on the instance. That is precisely why completed recordings are excluded from the backup category (they reference a media file on the source instance's disk and are not portable) -- the exclusion is not load-bearing on this fixture. The completed shape is documented from Dispatcharr's own apps/channels/tasks.py, which sets custom_properties['status'] = 'completed' alongside file_name / file_path keys naming a path under the source's recordings volume.
